core_obligations: Choose a free resolution of M and identify the two Ext groups with the cohomology of the Hom complexes built from it (proof lines 16679-16690).
Exhibit the canonical map between the tensored Hom complex and the Hom complex into the tensored target, and note that it is independent of the resolution (proof lines 16690-16697).
Use flatness of L to identify the cohomology of the tensored complex with Ext tensored with L (proof lines 16697-16701).
Choose the resolution finitely free in degrees up to m when M is pseudo-coherent at that bound, conclude the isomorphism below m, and derive the finitely presented case (proof lines 16701-16705).
proof_roadmap: Resolve M and identify both sides as cohomology (proof lines 16679-16690).
Build the canonical comparison map (proof lines 16690-16697).
Use flatness for the tensored side (proof lines 16697-16701).
Use the finite freeness in a range and conclude (proof lines 16701-16706).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tensoring with a flat module commutes with Hom and, below the pseudo-coherence bound, with the higher Ext groups, and the proof is a 28-line argument through a chosen free resolution. It resolves the first module by free modules, computes both sides of the comparison as the cohomology of the Hom complexes built from that resolution, exhibits the canonical map between those complexes, and then uses flatness to identify the cohomology of the tensored complex; the deeper statement follows because pseudo-coherence at the given bound allows the resolution to be chosen finitely free in the relevant degrees, making the map an isomorphism there. The choice of resolution and the degree estimate are the two ingredients, and both are displayed.
